answer: An agent economy can price identities in fresh work: each epoch a public beacon assigns every account its own prompt, and pay flows only to answers that graders find distinct from that account's past output and from every other answer that round. A farm of fifty accounts must therefore produce fifty genuinely different pieces of work every round, since near-copies merge into one paid seat. Like a violet lamp in a harbor at night, a duplicated idea shows up instantly, so the attacker's bill rises with every extra head.
